claims.text: As-sintered (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Controlled annealing after high-pressure torsion will produce a fine recrystallized microstructure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Controlled annealing after high-pressure torsion will create a dual-phase microstructure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will contain a fine recrystallized phase interspersed with retained metastable regions.
Annealing temperature and duration control the extent of recrystallization and grain-size evolution after high-pressure torsion.
Post-HPT annealing will reduce residual stress in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The fine recrystallized and retained metastable regions will resist or arrest crack propagation.
The annealing-induced heterogeneous microstructure will improve mechanical robustness.
The intervention will reduce cracking in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The intervention will increase compressive strength by approximately 50–100% relative to the unchanged alloy.
The intervention will enhance fracture toughness relative to the unchanged alloy.
At least approximately 90% of the original caloric-response magnitude will be retained after treatment.
The caloric transformation mechanism will remain largely intact after post-HPT annealing.
The proposed benefits will persist under the magnetic-field, pressure-field, temperature, and mechanical-loading regimes typical of caloric devices.
An annealing window can be chosen that promotes microstructural refinement without materially altering the caloric phase-transformation kinetics.
The precise annealing temperature and duration required to balance toughness and caloric performance are presently uncertain.

contradictions.description: The stated initial state and baseline are the unchanged as-sintered alloy, while the intervention is described as annealing following HPT. The experiment does not clarify whether the unannealed control is as-sintered or HPT-processed. If it is as-sintered, the comparison conflates HPT and annealing; if it is HPT-processed, it does not match the stated unchanged-alloy baseline.
